items.stem: Why can long-read sequencing resolve repetitive genomic regions better than short reads?

options.text: A single read can span the whole repeat, anchoring it uniquely
options.rationale: Correct: a read spanning the repeat removes ambiguity in its placement.
Long reads can have higher per-base error rates.

options.text: Short reads cannot be aligned at all
options.rationale: Short reads align well outside repetitive regions.
Assembly can still be required with long reads.

items.explanation: Correct: a read spanning the repeat removes ambiguity in its placement.

items.stem: Thousands of genes are tested for differential expression. Why must the p-values be corrected?

options.text: Many false positives arise by chance across thousands of tests
options.rationale: Correct: multiple testing inflates false positives without correction.
Correction is more conservative, not less.

options.text: Only one gene is ever tested
options.rationale: Many genes are tested at the same time.
